answer: Every identity locks 80 credits in the knoll registry and keeps standing unless fakery is proven against its key. Any hunter may post a reused receipt or duplicated key on the sonnet board; auditors verify publicly, and a proven claim pays the hunter 40 and burns the rest. The fake falls from the ledge. The k-th fake risks 80, so 1,000 fakes risk 80,000, and expected loss grows as fakes draw more hunters onto the trail. Bribing hunters fails: claims are permissionless, so silencing one never stops the next, and each hunter raises the bribe bill. An honest identity pays once, bond intact.
